items.title: Vietnam detains deputy agriculture minister in durian export probe - Free Malaysia Today
items.summary: ## The arrest marks the latest expansion in a probe centered on certification procedures for durian shipments to China. HANOI: Vietnamese police detained four people, including the deputy minister of agriculture and environment, on allegations of accepting bribes as part of an expanding investigation into corruption linked to durian exports to China. Deputy minister Hoang Trung is accused of abusing his position by issuing illegal policies, including allegedly creating “sub-licenses” to serve vested interests and generate “particularly large” illicit gains linked to durian exports, according to a statement on the public security ministry’s website. The alleged breaches caused “serious damage” to the legitimate rights and interests of durian growers and export businesses, resulting in “exceptionally” large losses to the state budget and “negatively” impacting the reputation of the entire Vietnamese agricultural sector, the statement said. The arrests mark the latest expansion in a probe centered on certification procedures for durian shipments to China involving the Center for Testing, Certification and Quality Services under the agriculture ministry, NhoNho Technology Co. and Thuy Fruit Co., according to the statement.

items.title: New subsea cables boost Intra-Asia connectivity - Light Reading
items.summary: The newly launched SEA-H2X and the upcoming SHV-HK subsea cables are strengthening the digital backbone between China and Southeast Asia. The Intra-Asia subsea cable route, particularly around Southeast Asia, has been a hive of activity as the subregion braces itself for the expected surge in bandwidth demand from AI workloads. China Mobile has announced that the 5,746 kilometer Southeast Asia-Hainan-Hong Kong (SEA-H2X) submarine cable system is now officially in commercial operation after a two-year delay. First announced in 2022, the subsea cable connects Hong Kong and Singapore and features links to Hainan in China, Songkhla in Thailand, and La Union in the Philippines. According to China Mobile, the commercial launch of the SEA-H2X submarine cable will play a pivotal role in establishing direct links between the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) and the Hainan Free Trade Port, as well as the main economies of Southeast Asia.

items.title: HAYA Therapeutics Receives FDA Fast Track Designation for HTX-001 - BioSpace
items.summary: # HAYA Therapeutics Receives FDA Fast Track Designation for HTX-001. *HTX-001 is in a Phase 1a/b trial and being developed for the treatment of nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM)*. LAUSANNE, Switzerland & SAN DIEGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--#Cardiology--HAYA Therapeutics SA, a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering precision RNA-guided therapeutics that target the regulatory genome to reprogram disease-driving cell states in common, chronic and age-related diseases, announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Fast Track Designation for HTX-001 for the treatment of symptomatic nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM). The first-in-class investigational long non-coding RNA (lncRNA)-targeting therapy is in a Phase 1a/b trial, with the first cohort dosed this past May. HTX-001 is a differentiated, potentially disease-modifying antisense oligonucleotide engineered to downregulate *WISPER*, a heart stress-specific lncRNA that is overexpressed in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, including nHCM. HAYA’s lead investigational candidate, HTX-001, is an antisense oligonucleotide targeting *WISPER*, and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1 clinical trial, initially for nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM).

items.title: Pakistan accused of fatally shooting 30 unarmed protesters in Kashmir - The Guardian
items.summary: At least 30 people are alleged to have been killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in the past two days as part of what has been claimed is a brutal state crackdown that has engulfed the disputed region for weeks. According to a local civil society group, Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), the Pakistani security services fired on tens of thousands of peaceful protesters, killing 25 people on Monday and five more on Tuesday. A wave of protests and violence in Pakistani Kashmir started in June. Amnesty International on Tuesday called for Pakistani authorities to lift the communications blackout. SA Khan, a spokesperson for JAAC, accused Pakistan’s security agencies of firing on unarmed protesters in Mirpur on Tuesday and then removing the evidence. A local resident in Mirpur, requesting anonymity for fear of retribution by the authorities, said the violence had erupted early on Tuesday afternoon when people gathered to protest against killings the previous day.
